newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain denies opposition report on arrests.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain denies opposition report on arrests.

text.p: Bahrain on Tuesday denied an opposition report that the Gulf Arab state had arrested children in connection with anti-government protests.
"The report is completely baseless," a government official told Reuters. "This has never happened. No child has been arrested," he added.
But the official confirmed that in general police arrest people who "take part in acts which violate security and stability and endanger citizens' interests and properties".

"If they are young, their parents are summoned to pledge that they will not repeat their acts of sabotage. Police then free them. This under no circumstances could be considered arrest," the official said.
The Bahrain Islamic Freedom Movement on Tuesday claimed that 20 Bahraini Shi'ite Moslems, mostly children, had been arrested this month.
It said in a statement sent to an international news organisation that three children, including six-year-old Sayyed Hussain Reda, were arrested in Adari village.
Three people in Sanabis village, five children in al-Daih village, two in Samaheej village and seven children aged between eight to 15 years in the small island of Sitra had been held, it said.
The London-based group did not say why they had been arrested but said another woman from Bilad al-Qadeem was shot and wounded on April 16.
Last month, the group claimed that Bahrain had arrested 19 people including children. Bahrain has also denied the claim.
Members of the island's majority Shi'ite community have waged sporadic protests, bombings and arson attacks since December 1994 to demand political and economic reforms by the Sunni-led government.
Around 28 people have been killed and hundreds arrested, including children.
